thinkers.thinker: Shahaf Armon, Efi Efrati, Raz Kupferman & Eran Sharon

pending.title: Small genera often grow large while large genera peak, decline and vanish
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin's geological generalization holds in the fossil record, then among well-sampled marine animal genera (a) genera that start small (1 or 2 valid species in their oldest 10-Myr bin) often grow to many species, and (b) extinct genera that become large (peak of 10 or more species) often peak and then decline before they vanish, and both patterns are more frequent than when the same genus's richness values are shuffled in time (so that they are not just an artifact of how range-through counts are built).

pending.title: Species in large genera differ from one another by small amounts
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin's remark (after Fries and Westwood) holds for insects, the amount of difference between species within a genus is smaller in larger genera: across insect genera, the mean pairwise COI-5P distance among congeneric species decreases with genus size (log10 of the number of described species in the genus), after removing differences between families.

pending.title: Overproduction makes a struggle for existence inevitable
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin is right that all organisms tend to increase at a geometrical rate but that increase is always checked (a struggle for existence), then in published matrix population models of wild, unmanipulated populations (a) most species show a population growth rate clearly above replacement in at least one of their populations or years (potential for geometric increase, lambda_max >= 1.05) and (b) almost no species shows sustained geometric growth over the whole of its record (geometric-mean lambda >= 1.10), because realized growth is held near replacement by limiting factors. This is tested separately for animals (COMADRE) and plants (COMPADRE).

pending.title: Very few species of past periods have living descendants
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin is right that 'very few' of the species of long-past geological periods now have living (modified) descendants, and that 'many whole orders, families and genera have died out entirely', then in the Paleobiology Database's record of fossil animals (Metazoa) only a small minority of the accepted genera that first appeared in the Paleozoic are still extant today, and a large share of the accepted families and orders that first appeared before the Cenozoic have no extant member.

pending.title: A single formation is likely shorter than the time needed to transform a species
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin is right that a single geological formation 'perhaps is short compared with the period requisite to change one species into another', then the typical duration of a fossil-bearing formation is a small fraction of the typical duration of a fossil species: the ratio R = median(formation duration) / median(species duration) is at most 0.5, where formation durations come from Macrostrat (North America) and species durations from the Paleobiology Database (marine bivalves).

pending.title: Land organisms change faster than marine organisms
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin is right that 'the productions of the land seem to change at a quicker rate than those of the sea', then fossil animal genera recorded from terrestrial environments in the Paleobiology Database turn over faster through the Phanerozoic than genera recorded from marine environments: in matched 10-million-year time bins, the per-capita turnover rate (the mean of the Foote boundary-crosser origination and extinction rates, per genus per million years) is higher for terrestrial than for marine genera, with a median paired difference d = (terrestrial - marine) above zero.

pending.title: A group's existence is continuous and it never reappears after disappearing
pending.hypothesis: DRAFT placeholder, to be refined in this run: internal gaps in the stratigraphic ranges of fossil genera and families in the Paleobiology Database are no more frequent than expected from sampling alone.

pending.title: In later geological periods new species have roughly balanced extinctions
pending.hypothesis: If Darwin is right that, 'looking to later times', the production of new forms has caused the extinction of about the same number of old forms, then across the Cenozoic stages (Danian to Piacenzian, 66 to 2.58 Ma) the per-capita origination of animal genera in the Paleobiology Database is approximately cancelled by per-capita extinction: the duration-weighted net diversification, expressed as a fraction of total turnover, B = sum[(p_i - q_i) dt_i] / sum[(p_i + q_i) dt_i], is close to zero (|B| <= 0.10), so standing diversity has not grown without limit.

pending.title: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape
pending.hypothesis: Octanol engages a planarian gap-junction channel better than hexanol does, consistent with the paper's premise that hexanol 'does not efficiently block gap junction channels'.

pending.title: Free energy is minimized only when every cell occupies a unique inferred place
pending.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, free-energy descent run to a steady state reaches the target form (every cell at its own distinct target location with the correct identity) from every initial condition tried, and no non-target stationary state has free energy at or below that of the target form.

pending.title: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
pending.hypothesis: In a coupled-cell bioelectric model of the anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula built with the paper's stated ingredients (Table 1 concentrations, 0.1x MMR medium, three regions whose K+/Cl- leak differences give a hyperpolarized neural tube near -50 mV and lateral neural folds/ectoderm near -5 mV, Kir channels, voltage-sensitive gap junctions) and BETSE's HCN2 kinetic model (V1/2 = -99 mV shifted +20 mV by cAMP, Na+:K+ permeability 0.2), adding homogeneously expressed HCN2 opens it preferentially in the hyperpolarized tube, drives tube cells further negative, and leaves the depolarized lateral regions essentially unchanged, i.e. it amplifies the existing Vmem gradient rather than shifting all regions uniformly.

pending.title: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
pending.hypothesis: The GYG->AAA mouse HCN2 construct used in the paper can still co-assemble with wild-type HCN2 subunits (the premise that makes it dominant-negative), so that a construct which fails to disrupt patterning can be read as evidence that native HCN2 activity is not required.

pending.title: Animal senses use the same ion channel mechanisms found in bacteria
pending.hypothesis: For each of the four senses named (touch, taste, temperature, hearing), at least one ion channel that transduces that sense in animals has a predicted structure containing the fold of a known bacterial ion channel, as measured by TM-score, clearly above the score a non-channel membrane protein reaches against the same bacterial channel.

pending.title: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
pending.hypothesis: In a voxel soft-body simulation where each contractile voxel's phase offset is random and fixed per clade (so selection can only change which voxels exist and which are contractile), selection for net displacement yields designs that move much farther than random designs under the same random actuation, and the gain depends on the evolved arrangement of passive and contractile voxels rather than on the particular phases.

pending.title: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
pending.hypothesis: Designs evolved for locomotion on simulated land with evolvable (finely tuned) actuation phases spend a large fraction of their evaluation airborne, whereas designs evolved with first-order hydrodynamics (reduced gravity plus surface drag) and random clade-fixed phase offsets stay in contact with the ground almost all the time, as living deciliated organisms do (93.3% vs 52.7% ground contact in the paper).

pending.title: Bilayer curvature from differential swelling (Timoshenko)
pending.hypothesis: If the Timoshenko bilayer law holds for a fabricated hydrogel bilayer, the change in curvature of a 3 mm wide, 30 mm long printed strip between the reference state (30 % relative humidity, 23 C) and equilibrium in water, predicted from independently measured layer thicknesses h1 and h2, moduli E1 and E2 and free swelling strains eps1 and eps2 of single-layer strips as kappa = 6(1+m)^2 / (h [3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))]) (eps1 - eps2) with m = h1/h2 and n = E1/E2, equals the measured change in curvature of the same bilayers; and the time to reach 1 - 1/e of the final curvature change scales as the square of the total thickness.

pending.title: Parastichy numbers change when the structure varies greatly in size
pending.hypothesis: In a Douady-Couder disc model (each new primordium placed at the global minimum, on the circle r = R0, of the summed repulsive energy of all existing primordia, which recede on a disc growing exponentially at rate G per plastochron), every attractor class with estimated basin measure above 0.01 at any growth parameter G in the sweep is one of the listed noble classes: constant divergence at the golden angle (137.5078 deg), constant divergence at the Lucas angle (99.5016 deg), or a bijugate period-2 divergence sequence (pi alternating with half the golden angle, 68.7539 deg, or with half the Lucas angle, 49.7508 deg). Secondary (claim-level, as mathematics only): the visible opposed parastichy pair of the dominant attractor rises as G falls, i.e. parastichy numbers vary with the size of the structure relative to the primordia, as thompson1917-ch14-05 states for sunflower discs.
